answer: Recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments enable agents to bridge disparate identity states into a verifiable nebula of unique assertions without leaking underlying metadata. By requiring each quill of submitted data to include a verifiable delay primitive, we impose a computational cost that ensures identity cloning becomes information-theoretically unforgeable. Staking collateral acts as a robust defense against collusion, where slashing penalties enforce a negative expected attack utility and stabilize the network at a resilient Nash equilibrium.
